title: 3.3.23 Arrays Checkpoint
description: Eight multiple-choice questions on arrays: changing items by index, loops and the off-by-one, push, pop, shift and unshift, split, arrays and functions, and nested arrays. Checked instantly.

questions.question: What does this print?
options: An error on the last round
questions.explanation: The array has 3 items, at indexes 0, 1 and 2, but `<=` lets `i` reach `3`. On that extra round `letters[3]` is one place past the end, so it prints `undefined`. Nothing crashes. Changing `<=` to `<` stops the loop in time.

questions.question: What does the last line print?
questions.explanation: `temps[1] = temps[0] + 10` replaces the `72` with `70`. Then `temps[2] = temps[1] - 8` reads that new `70` and stores `62` in the last place. Assigning by index changes an item in place and the array keeps its length.

questions.question: What does the last line print?
questions.explanation: `unshift("dee")` puts `dee` on the front, so the line is `dee, ana, bob, cy`. `shift()` takes `dee` back off the front and `push(served)` puts it on the back: `ana, bob, cy, dee`. So `line[0]` is `ana` and `line[3]` is `dee`.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: After the two pushes the array is `1, 2, 3, 4`. `pop()` removes the last item and hands it back, so `top` is `4`, and the array is left with `3` items.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: `addBonus` builds a brand new array in `result` and returns it. Nothing in it writes into `scores`, so `marks` still holds `70` and `80`, while `bumped` holds the new values `75` and `85`.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: `best` starts at `0`, and none of `4`, `9` or `6` is smaller than `0`, so it is never updated. The function returns `0`, a value that was never in the array. Starting from `numbers[0]` fixes it.

questions.question: What does the last line print?
questions.explanation: `grid[1][0] = 9` replaces the `4` (row 1, column 0) with `9`. `grid[0][2]` is the `3` at the end of the first row, so the sum is `3 + 9`, which is `12`. The first index picks the row and the second picks the item inside it.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: `split(",")` cuts the string at every comma, giving four pieces: `red`, `green`, `blue`, `teal`. So `parts.length` is `4` and `parts[2]`, counting from `0`, is `blue`.
